messages:
alex: quick sync  saw an incident where someone applied a 'pin override' to force traffic back to primary during an autofallback. audit shows the toggle but the rollout timeline still indicates fallback active and the metrics sampling dropped. this is confusing for oncall. can we tighten the UX?

maria: ugh. sounds like the console UI and the routing audit are out of sync. how do we currently record overrides?

todd: right now overrides are a simple flag saved on the rollout object with actor+reason but we don't surface a discrete transition in the timeline. the routing layer honors it immediately but dashboard logic prefers latest automatic trigger.

kai: proposal: treat operator overrides as first-class transitions. render them as a separate colored segment in the rollout bar with a small pill: "overridden by <actor> (ttl hh:mm)" and link to audit. also add an explicit "revert" control.

alex: agree. example problem: operator pins for 2h, then an automated fallback triggers later because of a race and the UI flips back without showing the manual action.

jordana: audit needs to be immutable and replayable. we should emit an event with a replay_token and policy snapshot that the forensic tool can feed into the simulator. ops-bot: replay-token:rt-1745560000 created.

todd: telemetry change: emit `rollout_action` events with fields encoded in the payload. sample: 

```
rollout_action = {
  "type": "override",
  "actor": "alex",
  "reason": "manual verification",
  "from": "fallback_v3",
  "to": "primary",
  "ttl_seconds": 7200,
  "policy_snapshot_id": "ps-abc123",
  "replay_token": "rt-1745560000"
}
```

kai: about TTLs: defaults matter. ops will often forget to set one. my suggestion: default TTL 60m, but surface a one-click extension menu (1h, 4h, indefinite with explicit risk warning). require a reason for >2h.

maria: also we should guard against flip-flop. when an operator creates an override, create a cooldown window where automatic triggers are suppressed for a configurable period unless the severity crosses an emergency threshold. show the cooldown countdown in the UI.

alex: how do we define "severity"? error rate? p95 latency? multiple signals?
jordana: allow policy rule to specify an override-escape condition: a set of absolute metrics that bypass cooldown. default: error_rate>0.2 OR p95_latency>2s. make it extensible.

todd: backend changes: persist policy_snapshot_id in event store. store full snapshot for every Nth event and diffs otherwise to control storage. provide an endpoint to fetch snapshot or replay a decision path using replay_token.

```http
POST /api/v1/rollouts/123/replay
{ "replay_token": "rt-1745560000" }
```

kai: UX microcopy: show clear badge: "Manual override (alex)  expires in 59m" with hover text: "This prevents autoswitches during cooldown unless emergency conditions met." include an undo icon.

maria: action items: todd will estimate storage+events, jordana will draft audit schema and replay API, kai will deliver mockups for timeline + pill + revert, i'll propose TTL defaults and escape thresholds. target: design doc by next Tue.

alex: thanks team. one last ask  can we make the API require a reason string when override_ttl_seconds > 3600? small friction but helps audits.

todd: will add server-side validation and a warn banner in the UI. ops-bot: note created: override-audit-proposal-1745560000.

alex: great, thanks :thumbsup:
